approaches_tried.approach: Verify OCR fixtures with a plain filled-rectangle image (no rendered text)
approaches_tried.reason: no OCR-recognizable content at all -- tesseract correctly found no text, so exit stayed 2 even after ocrmypdf ran; replaced with a fixture built by rendering real fitz text to a pixmap and inserting it as an image, per the plan's fallback fixture technique

approaches_tried.approach: Mask ocrmypdf off PATH via a plain PATH= override excluding its directory
approaches_tried.reason: on this NixOS profile bash/python3/every other tool also lives in the same /run/current-system/sw/bin directory, so excluding it broke bash's own shebang resolution; replaced with a scratch bin dir of symlinks to every real PATH entry except ocrmypdf/tesseract

findings: IMPORTANT for Phase 4: pymupdf4llm.to_markdown()'s force_text=True default (unrelated to this task, pre-existing) makes the PRIMARY tier silently invoke Tesseract directly via PyMuPDF's own textpage-OCR API whenever a page has no extractable text and tesseract is on PATH -- observed recovering full correct text from the render-to-pixmap fixture under LITERATURE_CONVERTER=auto with the venv provisioned, producing exit 0 instead of the expected exit 2. This is a DIFFERENT code path than the ocrmypdf CLI this phase adds (the 'never invokes ocrmypdf' guarantee holds regardless), but it means an unforced `auto` run is not a reliable exit-2 trigger on a machine with both the primary-tier venv and tesseract present. Phase 4's auto-exits-2 regression test should force the primary tier unavailable (e.g. LITERATURE_PYENV_DIR pointed at a scratch/nonexistent directory) to get a deterministic exit-2 assertion, mirroring how auto degrades to the mandatory fallback tier (which has no such internal OCR trigger) on any machine without a provisioned venv.
